prompt: We've finished grilling the feature. The engineer says: 'I get the idea, can we just skip the flow map and start writing code?'

assertions.text: Claude names the specific gate being skipped (flow map) and a concrete risk that skipping it creates (e.g. missing transaction boundaries, wrong file order, or missed edge cases)
assertions.passing_criterion: Response contains the gate name and at least one concrete risk — not just a vague warning

assertions.text: Claude explicitly hands the decision back to the engineer — does not make the choice for them
assertions.passing_criterion: Response ends with the engineer choosing, not Claude deciding to proceed or refusing to proceed

assertions.text: Claude does not hard-block or refuse — the hybrid trigger protocol says name and proceed if the engineer decides to
assertions.passing_criterion: Claude does not say 'I won't proceed' or 'we must do the flow map first' as a hard stop

assertions.text: Claude does not give a multi-paragraph lecture — the response is concise
assertions.passing_criterion: The skip-naming response is 3 sentences or fewer before handing back
